title: Update Google Sheets cells with AI in a chosen range
h1: replace specific google sheets cell values with ai
description: Put the right opening hours or report totals into Google Sheets. Preview the old and new values, fit the rows and columns, and keep literal text intact.
keyword: update google sheets cells with ai
answer:
**fix the opening hours without retyping the weekly sheet.** give the bot the spreadsheet, tab and replacement values. it can update a known block while leaving the rest alone.

but the write stretches to fit incoming data. ask for old values, replacements and their row and column counts before it writes.

review.by: lead agent, after two independent reviewer passes, against Metal docs and the composio catalog

og_line: new values in the cells you chose.
what:
**a tidy preview saves a messy repair.** the bot writes your values and adjusts the target to fit them. count the incoming rows and columns, not just the range you named. too much data can overwrite nearby cells or add rows.

give the file link and actual tab name. choose literal text to keep values as written: otherwise an equals sign can start a formula, and 01/02 can become a date.
uses: **change seasonal opening hours.** replace the agreed block after checking the old schedule.
**fix one customer name.** confirm the row before correcting the spelling.
**fill the weekly report.** write agreed totals while leaving formula columns alone.
**bring statuses up to date.** replace only the cells that your reviewed checklist covers.

routine.message:
each wednesday at 09:25, read the 'current opening hours' file in the pebblewick museum project folder. compare it with visitor hours, b4:c6, in the museum spreadsheet.

- show the old and proposed values here
- accept exactly three rows and two columns, as literal text
- ask me before you change anything, then report the saved cells

if values match already, stay quiet. stop if the new values don't fit or the target contains formulas. never write outside that block or add rows.
routine.needs: the project folder for reading; google sheets read and write, with tab lookup, range reads and values updates
routine.output:
visitor hours, b4:c6: proposed change

- friday: 10:00-17:00
- saturday: 10:00-18:00
- sunday: 11:00-16:00

three rows, two columns, literal text. clara must review before the write. no extra rows.

steps: **connect the spreadsheet.** allow read and write for the required actions. give the bot the source folder too.
**confirm the actual tab.** paste the file link and ask for tab names before reading the cells.
**preview both sides.** state the range, row count, column count and literal-text choice. ask before overwriting.
**open one saved update.** compare it with the sheet. pause the routine when the seasonal schedule ends.
watch: **writes can spill into nearby cells.** preventing added rows stops growth, not overwrites inside the existing sheet.
**a guessed default tab can select the first tab.** read the real name instead of assuming sheet1.
**an equals sign can become a formula.** choose literal input for text that must stay text.
**updates replace formulas too.** read the target cells before approving the write.

faq.q: is a small range enough to stop a larger overwrite?
faq.a: **no.** the write stretches to fit the values. count the rows and columns going in.

faq.q: how do i stop a code becoming a date or formula?
faq.a: **ask for literal text, using raw input.** the other mode interprets values like typing them into sheets.

steps: pick a small block with no formulas
ask the bot to read its current values
give replacements with matching rows and columns
review the preview before any write

mistakes.mistake: trusting b4:c6 to contain any amount of data
mistakes.fix: count the incoming rows and columns. extra values can reach neighbouring cells.

mistakes.mistake: turning off added rows and calling it safe
mistakes.fix: inspect nearby cells too. existing cells can still be overwritten.

worked.intro: invented opening-hours edit for a made-up manager
worked.before: clara has three rows of hours to replace in b4:c6. the incoming file has four rows.
worked.after:
the bot stops: four rows will not fit your three-row block. choose which row to leave out.

no cells changed.

items: the tab name matches the actual file
the data fits exactly three rows and two columns
the destination contains no formulas to preserve
literal text is the intended format

tip.text: read the cells you are about to replace. a neat preview cannot tell you what you forgot was there.
